question: Can the Western pre-1980 forms nehualíame/newalime be independently anchored in the Rarámuri lexical family meaning 'make/do' without inferring their internal morphology from the bilingual book title alone?

evidence.source: Manual Ralámuli Escrito para Todas y Todos, UPNECH 2019
evidence.source_access: institutional existence/authorship verified in UPNECH and Chihuahua government; exact multivariety table consulted through an indexed digital copy
evidence.assessment: Directly anchors newá-/newálime and regional cognates in the semantic domain 'hacer'.

evidence.source: Government of Chihuahua, Sekáti Newárame festival announcements, 2018/2024
evidence.assessment: Independent official use supports the broader newa- 'make/produce' lexical-derivational family, though Newárame is not assumed to have the same morphology as newálime.

evidence.source: Western Rarámuri book title, Albino Mares Trías 1972
evidence.spanish_title: Hacemos Muchas Cosas con el Mezcal
evidence.assessment: Whole-title alignment alone did not permit a word-level gloss; the 2019 multivariety evidence now independently makes a 'hacer' analysis for the newa-/nehua- family well motivated.

evidence.spanish_title: Con el maíz se pueden hacer muchas cosas
evidence.assessment: A second Western title repeats the constructional environment and transparently belongs to the same newa- family, but the internal suffixal analysis remains to be established independently.

formal_comparison.interpretation: The lexical base associated with 'hacer' is secure; the historical/dialectal relation among the endings requires a separate morphological audit.

claims_supported: newá- is a multivariety Rarámuri lexical family in the semantic domain 'hacer/elaborar'.
Western newálime is explicitly aligned with Spanish hacer in the 2019 multivariety manual.
The 1972 and 2010 Western title forms nehualíame/newalime can now be linked to that lexical family without deriving the gloss solely from their Spanish titles.
claims_not_supported: That the ending of newálime is synchronically or historically identical to participial -ame.
That nehualíame, newalime and newálime are orthographically identical representations rather than dialectal/historical variants requiring analysis.
A word-by-word segmentation of the 1972 or 2010 titles.
next_steps: Audit the morphology of newálime/newáliwi/newáliwa using grammars and paradigms.
Search pre-1980 Western materials for the base newa- without the target ending.
Test whether the spelling nehualíame reflects an older orthography for newalime or additional phonological/morphological material.
